The night train left the city exactly on time. Most of the passengers were already asleep before the last suburb slid past the windows.

In the dining car a waiter polished glasses that nobody would use. He liked the quiet hours best, when the rails sang and the lamps swayed.

Somewhere past midnight the train slowed for a single lit platform in the snow. No one got on, and no one got off.
